**Trader consensus centers on 30–32°C as the most likely range for Panama City’s daily maximum on August 15, 2026, reflecting the city’s tropical wet-season climatology and current forecast guidance.** 

Panama City lies at low latitude with strong, consistent insolation year-round, but August falls in the peak rainy season when the Intertropical Convergence Zone drives frequent afternoon convection. This produces widespread cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and evaporative cooling that typically caps daytime highs near the long-term average of 29–30 °C. Official and model guidance for the date shows maxima clustering around 30–31 °C, with brief windows for 32 °C if convective activity is delayed or less intense. 

Higher outcomes (33 °C+) remain low-probability because sustained clear skies and stronger insolation are uncommon in mid-August, while cooler readings (≤29 °C) would require unusually early or widespread rain. Recent model runs and observational trends have reinforced this narrow band, leading traders to assign the bulk of probability mass to the central values that align with both climatology and the latest forecast consensus.
